role: Assume H: every odd integer n>1 has a standard Collatz iterate T^k(n) that is a positive integer strictly below n. Prove that H would imply that every positive integer reaches 1. Distinguish proving the implication from proving H.
public_findings: Assume H. We prove by strong induction on n that every positive integer n reaches 1 under the standard Collatz map. Base case: n=1 already equals 1. Inductive step: let n>1 and assume every positive integer m<n reaches 1. If n is even, then T(n)=n/2<n, so the induction hypothesis shows that n/2, and hence n, reaches 1. If n is odd, H supplies some k such that m=T^k(n) is positive and m<n. By the induction hypothesis, m reaches 1; appending that trajectory to the first k iterates from n shows that n reaches 1. Thus, conditional on H, every positive integer reaches 1. This proves only the implication H => the stated Collatz conclusion; it does not prove H itself.

assumptions: Standard Collatz map on positive integers: T(n)=n/2 for even n, T(n)=3n+1 for odd n.
v2(m) is the largest k>=0 with 2^k dividing positive integer m.
